channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal trade sustains families as tree loss threatens food security
item.description: A 65-year-old burner says his family depends on the work, while an environmental agency director warns that producers are cutting orange and mango trees.

item.title: Sierra Leone analyst says vice presidency has no path to power
item.description: Foday M. Daboh argues that successive governments have used the office to balance party interests, leaving vice presidents without a clear route to succession.

item.title: Cape Verde drops three places to 71st in FIFA ranking
item.description: The team remains the highest-ranked Portuguese-speaking country, with 1,360.08 points in the latest update.

item.title: Guinea orders distributors to remove Burkina Faso’s RTB channel
item.description: The communications regulator says the public broadcaster aired an editorial it judged hostile to Guinea and a caricature targeting the president.

item.title: Eenhana opens N$2.5m market for 30 informal traders
item.description: The stalls beside Eenhana District Hospital were funded by the Social Security Commission and the Ministry of Urban and Rural Development.

item.title: Cameroon's minister orders mayors to issue birth certificates to election candidates
item.description: Georges Elanga Obam says refusing the documents or charging fees for them taints the electoral contest, and the rule is that they are free.

item.title: Namibia starts second FMD vaccination round in //Kharas
item.description: Veterinary teams began the campaign on 16 November, as the outbreak remained at 131 confirmed cases across 18 farms.

item.title: Senegal continues search for dozens missing after migrant boat capsizes
item.description: A survivor told police about 100 people, including five women, were aboard the boat that washed ashore near Yenne.

item.title: Benin fuel depots blame station queues on distribution delays
item.description: Depot director Sosthène H. Mesmin Hounsou says stocks remain available, while higher demand strains station staff, trucks and delivery schedules.

item.title: NCBA Bank and MTN MoMo launch USh140m MoKash rewards campaign
item.description: The 12-week promotion rewards customers for loan repayments, savings balances and clearing eligible debts, running through February 16, 2027.

item.title: Kenya names bidders for three mineral projects, pending licences
item.description: A US-led consortium won the Mrima Hill tender, while a Chinese joint venture was chosen for projects in Samburu and Tharaka Nithi.

item.title: Tambura clashes displace 300 households to camps and nearby communities
item.description: Officials report 100 households in Maboiku and 200 in Sinawiri as South Sudan's government plans an assessment of those who fled.

item.title: Senegal investigators refer two Omega Pro-linked people over fund collection
item.description: A complainant says she handed over four cheques totalling CFA31.56 million after being promised returns of up to 300%.

item.title: Tunisia opts for a separate financial structure for postal bank
item.description: The proposed entity would offer easier-term banking services to some social groups without converting the postal service into a conventional bank.

item.title: Sirleaf warns Liberia’s peace faces risks without unity and inclusion
item.description: The former president said 23 years without war could be undone if leaders fail to provide equal opportunity, as opposition figures face prosecutions.

item.title: Togo hospitals lift medicine availability to 99% under management reform
item.description: Across nine facilities, indicators rose 110% from 2017 to September 2026, while officials face the task of sustaining the gains.

item.title: Cape Verde pledges FIC venues in Mindelo and Praia
item.description: Prime Minister Francisco Tavares said the next editions will use sites owned by the fair, which has struggled with space in both cities.

item.title: South Africa inflation climbs to 5.2% as fuel and vegetable costs rise
item.description: Statistics South Africa says fuel inflation accelerated to 42.9%, while vegetable prices rose 8.1% year on year in October.

item.title: South C residents demand safety report on 15-storey apartments
item.description: The residents say Bridge Port Apartments was approved for 10 floors and its pillars were damaged when a neighbouring building collapsed in January.

item.title: Three Republicans urge US Treasury to balance Rwanda sanctions
item.description: Their request follows US sanctions imposed only on Rwanda over its role in destabilising eastern DR Congo.

item.title: South Sudan offers 14 oil blocks to investors
item.description: The government targets crude output above 200,000 barrels a day within two years, from current production of about 174,000 to 175,000.

item.title: National Bank of Malawi supports 15 MUST students with awards
item.description: The students received scholarships and academic excellence awards on Tuesday through the bank’s Mo Excellence Programme.

item.title: Pasteur Institute of Tunis starts amphitheatre renovation
item.description: Backed by the Dr Sadok Besrour Foundation and Unesco, the work will upgrade audiovisual systems, ventilation and accessibility while preserving the building’s character.

item.title: Ghana’s Black Challenge beat USA 3-1 to reach Amputee World Cup quarter-finals
item.description: The national team scored once before half-time and twice after the break, setting up a match with Egypt on Thursday in Mexico.

item.title: Liberia's Justice Ministry misses court deadline to free vessel and seven crew
item.description: A judge ordered the IB Atlantic IV and its seven crew released by 4 p.m. Wednesday, but they were still in state custody that evening.

item.title: Liberia launches its first written foreign policy
item.description: The document includes a gender-responsive policy that the government says is Africa’s first formally adopted and launched written version.

item.title: Lutheran World Federation sells off nine containers and aluminium profiles
item.description: Sealed bids for the nine containers and nine types of aluminium profiles close on 10 December in Addis Ababa.

item.title: NSIA Banque mobilises €100 million facility for Ivorian businesses
item.description: The syndicated credit line targets small and medium-sized enterprises, women-led firms and energy-transition projects, but access terms remain unpublished.

item.title: Bangui pro-government march draws only a handful of onlookers
item.description: The event on Independence Avenue paired a march with music, while government spokesman Évariste Ngamana criticised the BRDC’s mobilisation.

item.title: Absa trains up to 150 Makola traders in money management
item.description: The bank’s Compliance volunteers discussed savings and financial resilience, and showed traders how to handle Ghana cedi notes.

item.title: Mali dismantles Bamako site as 487 expelled from Guinea await return
item.description: Authorities have moved 467 people to a Ouinzindougou hostel while 20 Burkinabè remain at Kouremalé, pending return arrangements with their governments.

item.title: Egypt directs $1.5 billion IMF tranche to central bank reserves
item.description: The final review clears a combined $2.3 billion disbursement, including $800 million for green, water-management and renewable-energy reforms.

item.title: African Union deploys election expert to South Sudan ahead of February 2027 polls
item.description: The expert will support the National Elections Commission while voter registration continues across the country’s 10 states and three administrative areas.

item.title: Tunisia's sports minister unveils football reform after two decades of failings
item.description: Sadok Mourali outlined a long-term overhaul of youth training, elite funding and stadium repairs after MPs demanded the football federation's board step down.

item.title: Sonangol identifies pre-salt oil in Angola’s Kwanza Basin
item.description: The Burututu-1 well is the first in Block 5/06 to find hydrocarbons in pre-salt reservoirs, but the discovery’s commercial scale is unknown.

item.title: Tunisia forecasts overnight storms in the far North-West
item.description: The meteorological institute expects daytime highs of 26°C to 31°C across most regions, reaching 33°C locally in the Centre.

item.title: Seed-Co puts US$20,000 into Lilongwe golf tournament
item.description: About 500 golfers are expected at the four-day championship, with players coming from Malawi and four other African countries.

item.title: Lee Shim accuses Mauritius officials of conspiracy over racing and betting
item.description: The 72-year-old filed a police complaint naming the attorney general, the Financial Crimes Commission chief and Kulwant Kumar Ubheeram.

item.title: Mauritius health minister warns stigma deters HIV testing and care
item.description: Anil Bachoo says fear of rejection keeps some people from testing, attending clinics and continuing treatment.

item.title: Angolan farm wins place in 15-country business awards final
item.description: Fazenda Agrícola – NR will represent Angola in Johannesburg on 25 November after winning the first Standard Bank awards in the country.

item.title: Fire destroys records and equipment at Kindia education office
item.description: The fire damaged the prefectural director’s office after reported electricity-supply disruptions, and investigations are pending.

item.title: Tunisia's finance committee approves seven water project bills
item.description: The bills cover loans, guarantees and additional financing for projects to strengthen water resources and upgrade drinking-water infrastructure.

item.title: Uganda lenders urged to address USh31.4 trillion small-business gap
item.description: At a Kampala meeting, financial institutions were asked to connect available investment capital with businesses that struggle to qualify for formal loans.

item.title: Mali’s army frees 24 detained soldiers near Kidal
item.description: The soldiers were taken to Gao after a coordinated operation by the army and its partners in In-Tebezas on Wednesday.

item.title: Comoros reports 602 Force jeunes beneficiaries and 100 dairy cows
item.description: Agriculture Minister Daniel Ali Bandar said 483 beneficiaries are in Ngazidja and 119 in Ndzuani, while Mwali applications remain under review.

item.title: Sudanese court orders Hemedti and 13 others to pay 1.03 trillion pounds
item.description: The 14 defendants were sentenced to death in absentia over the looting and destruction of medical supplies facilities in six states.

item.title: Malawi's governing party has left 90% of manifesto promises unstarted, assessment finds
item.description: An assessment of the Democratic Progressive Party's 2025-30 manifesto was published a year after the party won power in Malawi's September 2025 elections.

item.title: Zambian graduate with disability lands job after approaching minister
item.description: Blessings Mulumbu, a University of Zambia graduate who uses a wheelchair, stopped Community Development Minister Sheal Mulyata at a community inclusion conference.

item.title: Mauritius civic programme teaches 200 students how government works
item.description: Students from 106 schools visited the National Assembly and Bank of Mauritius before studying the Constitution and the roles of state institutions.

item.title: Malawi's gold push faces mercury risks in four districts
item.description: Industry players say informal miners use toxic mercury to process reef gold, raising concerns about harm to workers and surrounding communities.

item.title: South Sudan launches accountants' institute with two diploma levels
item.description: The Institute of Certified Public Accountants of South Sudan says it plans to develop a full certification course from next year.

item.title: Blue Nile activists urge restart of suspended emergency rooms
item.description: Volunteers say the rooms had delivered food, shelter materials and other support as renewed displacement strains local relief services.

item.title: Mozambique approves ExxonMobil's amended Rovuma LNG plan
item.description: The cabinet cleared changes to the Area 4 project, removing a regulatory obstacle before the company's planned investment decision this year.

item.title: Tanzania tells officials to use AI without replacing expertise
item.description: At a three-day Morogoro course, the government called for verified information, data security and professional standards in AI use.

item.title: Zimbabwe power utility says network overhaul needs US$2.4 billion
item.description: ZETDC says two decades of underfunding left transmission and distribution assets short of maintenance, refurbishment and expansion.

item.title: Zimbabwean gamers see streaming chance in GTA VI launch
item.description: The first major Grand Theft Auto (GTA) instalment since GTA V, released more than a decade ago, lands on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

item.title: Tinubu expands 2027 campaign itinerary to 19 states and Abuja
item.description: The revised schedule adds several locations to the president's original campaign plan, according to Premium Times.

item.title: Al Salam Bank Algeria offers firms leasing for equipment and premises
item.description: The Islamic bank pitched its financing, leasing and digital services at the TASSHIIL 2026 investment fair in Algiers.

item.title: Lomé bulldozers clear traders’ stalls before 20 November deadline
item.description: Traders using pavements and public spaces had been told to leave by 20 November, but machinery began clearing the areas at the start of the month.

item.title: Burundi falls to Zambia after Bimenyimana’s 78th-minute goal
item.description: The substitute scored from Girumugisha’s pass, two minutes after entering, in a match that was 0-0 at half-time.

item.title: Farage urges UK prime minister to block Chagos sovereignty transfer
item.description: The Reform UK leader rejects Mauritius’s claim as Port Louis seeks a roadmap by December 2026 to ratify the May 2025 treaty.

item.title: DR Congo's mining sector gives $1.1 million to Ebola response
item.description: The money was handed to the coordination body for the country's 17th Ebola wave, as the World Health Organization said the outbreak remains an international emergency six months.

item.title: Cameroon's chamber seeks processing partnerships and more reliable power
item.description: At a Yaounde forum, the chamber also urged clearer approval timelines and regulatory rules to help firms assess investment risks.

item.title: Standard Bank entered Uganda by acquiring Grindlays in 1991
item.description: Journalist Michael Wakabi recalls the deal as other banks were closing branches or leaving a market facing slow economic recovery.

item.title: Naira firms slightly in official market as parallel rate stays above N1,440
item.description: The official interbank rate stood at N1,350.50 to the dollar early on Thursday, while street dealers in Lagos and Abuja quoted between N1,445 and N1,468.

item.title: Madagascar launches $250 million electricity programme tied to results
item.description: The ASCENT programme, funded by the World Bank, aims to bring better power access and modern cooking to more than 2.5 million people by 2030.

item.title: Burkinabè abroad give CFA7 million to national fund
item.description: Donors in Central Africa and Belgium delivered the money to the foreign minister, with CFA4 million raised at a Belgian cultural festival.

item.title: Zambian hospital completes two kidney transplants and targets 50 a year
item.description: A wife travelled with her husband from Copperbelt Province to Lusaka to donate a kidney, while a 56-year-old man received one from his son.

item.title: Newmont tops Ghana Club 100 as Mahama urges firms to compete for $10 billion programme
item.description: MTN Ghana’s operator placed second and Gold Fields third; Mahama said private companies would implement the government programme.

item.title: Tebboune cites 520 fictitious import firms as Algeria tightens checks
item.description: The president said 90 companies were registered at one address and acknowledged that stricter controls are also weighing on honest operators.

item.title: Eritrea and Ethiopia trade artillery fire near disputed Badme border town
item.description: The Armed Conflict Location and Event Data project (ACLED), a conflict monitor, says both sides have mobilised heavily along the border.

item.title: Senegal's MPs reject 2027 budget, stopping review of remaining sections
item.description: The National Assembly voted 126 to 18 against the first section, covering revenue and debt, leaving the rest of the budget unexamined.

item.title: Bank of Ghana puts Justice Annie Ruth Jiagge on new GH¢10 note
item.description: The judge appears on the green note in the Heritage Series, which enters circulation from December 1; existing notes remain legal tender.

item.title: UN rights office records 694 violations in DR Congo in September
item.description: The tally rose by more than 41 % from August, with provinces affected by armed conflict accounting for 91 % of documented violations.

item.title: Antananarivo moves public-transport stops around Analakely and Soarano
item.description: The city says the temporary changes will make room for a road project and ease congestion ahead of the holiday season.

item.title: Tinubu receives state police amendment bill for assent
item.description: The Justice Ministry is validating operational guidelines, which a presidential working group will review before presenting them to the president.

item.title: Benin presents dual-apprenticeship model at African skills forum
item.description: At a ministerial roundtable in Oran, Awaou Baco described national qualifications and a unified ministry linking training, employment and business.

item.title: Ghana and Norway agree to expand maritime and oil investment
item.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa said the governments will also support digital-economy startups and accelerate work on a tax treaty.

item.title: Benin allocates CFA11,59 billion to digital ministry for 2027
item.description: Minister Mahuna Akplogan presented the plan to lawmakers, with two-thirds of the money earmarked for investment in public services, connectivity and innovation.

item.title: Zambia hands K2.8 million school buildings to Malundu pupils
item.description: Until now, Malundu Community School's lessons were held under a tree and, at times, in neighbouring churches, district commissioner Joel Mboyoma said.

item.title: Malawi medical referrals cost K43.4 billion a year
item.description: Reserve Bank records show K16 billion went to treatment abroad from March to July 2026, while a professor estimates wider costs are higher.

item.title: US ambassador reaffirms position on Western Sahara after UN mission ends
item.description: Mike Waltz met Morocco’s foreign minister, head of government and former head of the UN mission during a visit on 17 November.

item.title: Air Mauritius diverts Mauritius-New Delhi flight to Mumbai
item.description: The airline said a technical fault may have caused the diversion, but its communications chief had not yet confirmed the circumstances.

item.title: Ravinala Airports and Okalou bring Light Festival to Ivato
item.description: The 21 November programme combines family shows, performances by Nate Tex, Mage 4 and Big MJ (a Malagasy rapper and performer), and a light show at 18:30.

item.title: Madagascar renames international karting trophy for Faly Andrianafetra
item.description: The competition's 26th edition is scheduled for 22 November 2026 at the SRK circuit in Imerintsiatosika, and counts toward the national championship.

item.title: Madagascar court hears Ambohimalaza accused as trial opens
item.description: Fenohasina denied accusations over a 2025 birthday party linked to the deaths of 35 people, while nearly 50 civil parties seek compensation.

item.title: Koryx values Namibia’s Haib copper project at US$2.5 billion
item.description: The pre-feasibility study projects 130 000 tonnes of payable copper a year in the mine’s first 10 years and targets early construction works in 2027.

item.title: Namibia tracks 71% of Sustainable Development Goal indicators
item.description: The statistics agency’s 2025 framework covers 176 of 248 measures, up from 66.4% in 2019, but leaves gaps in three goals.

item.title: Eswatini deputy master warns against reversing Royal Swazi property sales
item.description: Lindelwa Magagula told the High Court that undoing land sales and a mortgage payment could cost emaSwati jobs and the country tax revenue.

item.title: UN committee urges Eswatini to adopt national jobs policy
item.description: The recommendation follows concerns that youth unemployment reached 58.2% and that existing programmes are not producing sustainable work.

item.title: EWADE pegs first Mkhondvo-Ngwavuma phase at E6.06 billion
item.description: The estimate covers four infrastructure components; a proposed E987 million BADEA loan still needs parliamentary approval.

item.title: Mbabane Swallows reports financial strain before Sunday league clash
item.description: The club says it has no sponsor for salaries and other expenses, while players reportedly refused to train after transport and meal problems.

item.title: Egypt and Syria sign aviation deal after 14 years without direct flights
item.description: The agreement enables technical exchanges and airport-procedure work, while Egyptian authorities have inspected Damascus and Aleppo airports.

item.title: Poll shows Barrow ahead by a narrow margin in Gambia's three-way race
item.description: The survey by civil society group Gambia Participates found 19% of voters undecided ahead of the 5 December 2026 election.

item.title: Rwanda and Uganda launch three-year police plan against cross-border crime
item.description: The programme sets out joint investigations, intelligence-sharing and coordinated operations against trafficking, terrorism, smuggling and cybercrime.

item.title: Sirte civil service branch honors 24 workers and three institutions
item.description: The Sirte Medical Reference Laboratory took first place, followed by Ibn Sina Teaching Hospital and the Sirte Oncology Center.

item.title: GBoS urges review of 2005 Statistics Act for next year
item.description: Deputy Statistician-General Alieu Saho says the law predates smartphones, big data and artificial intelligence and leaves data-sharing rules unclear.

item.title: Rwanda's defence minister holds talks at Brussels security forum
item.description: Juvenal Marizamunda met government officials and international organisations at the European Union's security forum, which drew delegates from more than 80 partner countries.

item.title: Morocco targets 50,000 defense-industry jobs and 65% export revenue by 2035
item.description: The roadmap also sets a goal for local industry to meet about 40% of the armed forces’ and security agencies’ needs.

item.title: Lake Chad experts urge customs reforms for cross-border trade
item.description: The proposed changes include one-stop border posts and rules tailored to small businesses as insecurity and informal trade constrain a market of about 30 million people.
